text:
sam_support: seeing multiple customer 503s starting ~08:12 UTC. spike in hosted-infer errors, customers report timeouts and toolcall failures. attaching a quick summary and logs.
maya_ops: thanks — noticed a pattern: upstream inference worker containers restarted around the same time. 3 distinct hosts showing rapid restarts.
jon_eng: any crashlogs / coredumps? can you paste the last lines from the runner logs?
sam_support: paste from one host: 
```
[2026-03-17T08:12:35Z] infer-runner[pid=2431]: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f9a1c... sp 0x7ffea... error 4 in libattn.so
[2026-03-17T08:12:36Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2431 (infer-runner) score 999 or sacrifice child
[2026-03-17T08:12:36Z] infer-runner: terminated by signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
```
jon_eng: segfault + OOM in same window. sounds like memory blowup during a batched streaming session. what model and batch sizes were active?
maya_ops: traffic trace shows a few long-context streaming sessions from a single customer that had bursts of concurrent tool calls -> QPS spike + big sequence lengths. Many requests pinned to the same worker due to routing.
li_devops: deploybot reported a capacity autoscale event at 08:11:58, then 5 worker containers were created, two immediately restarted. logs show `nvml: out of memory` on one host.
eve_sre: our fallback routing didn't kick in for one tenant — requests retried and piled up, exacerbating memory pressure. need to confirm cache/KV sizes.
jon_eng: repro plan: reproduce locally with same model + long sequence + toolcall payload. steps: 1) run small harness with continuous batching enabled; 2) spawn 8 concurrent streaming sessions with context ~16k tokens; 3) ensure `KV_PREFETCH=on` to match hosted config; 4) monitor `/proc/<pid>/maps` and nvml for memory growth.
maya_ops: did we see any recent runtime change? last prod deploy was 08:05 — a kernel update?
li_devops: no kernel changes. we rolled a runtime patch at 07:58 that changed KV cache eviction heuristics (PR #839). rolling that back to test.
sam_support: customers asking about billing and auth: some experienced double-billing for failed requests. 2 customers opened support tickets.
eve_sre: escalate billing: mark impacted requests as failed-without-charge and flag for finance. ping @billing-team.
jon_eng: initial hypothesis: under high-concurrency long-context streaming, KV prefetch + changed eviction interaction causes unbounded resident growth -> OOM -> segfault on corrupted mem. need heap/valgrind-ish snapshot or address sanitizer build.
li_devops: can we attach gcore on a reproducer before it crashes? gcore increases memory but helps postmortem. also capture `nvidia-smi dmon` and `nvml` counters.
maya_ops: I've kicked off a canary rollback of PR #839 to a small zone. early signs: one host stabilized, no restarts in 6 minutes.
sam_support: interim mitigation: 1) throttle long-context streaming concurrency per-tenant, 2) enforce per-worker in-flight request limit, 3) enable fallback routing to dedicated pool.
eve_sre: config flags pushed: `MAX_STREAM_CONCURRENCY=4` and `ENABLE_FALLBACK=true` for hosted. monitoring dashboards showing p95 latency dropping and restart count falling. :thumbsup:
jon_eng: next steps: build address-sanitizer variant of runtime, reproduce with the harness, verify root cause (KV free-after-use or kernel race), then craft a fix. also add preventive telemetry: resident set tracking, kv-cache-growth alerts, and per-worker crash counters.
li_devops: collecting artifacts: gcore x3, nvml logs, runner stack traces, and docker event timelines -> uploading to S3 `s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/1759854321/`.
sam_support: updating CS tickets and telling customers: mitigation in place, avoiding billing for failed attempts, ETA for root cause analysis ~24-48h.
deploybot: autoscale event: created 5 workers at 2026-03-17T08:11:58Z, restarts detected on hosts gpu-12 and gpu-14 at 08:12:36Z.
maya_ops: leaving this thread to continue investigation in #eng-runtime but will post final RCA here. thanks everyone. :heart:
